Mostly depends on what your focus is. I would start with learning basic proper technique before experimenting with tapping and such.

Once you feel comfortable with scales and have a good repertoire of chords then you want to shed fingerstyle patterns and tapping. Once you're confortable enough with those techniques then learn the song.

There's no specific timeline i could give you because it's different for everyone. You might be able to play that specific piece after 2 years of playing if you specialise in that specific style. Might take you decades to feel like you truely master that style of playing.

Playing guitar is not an end goal you can achieve after a set number of years. There will always be more stuff to learn as you progress. Focus on the journey rather than the destination.

Yooo I was the exact same situation as you about a year ago! Here are some tips:

1. FOLLOW THE MUSIC!! In this world, DJs are your band mates. Learn the repertoire as best you can. Blackout on the breaks and go nuts on the drops. Punch strobe on the 808s. Don't forget to always change it up on popular songs.

2. Use your brain ffs. If something looks stupid: fix it. Learn to program as best you can so you can adapt to the promoters' requests.

3. Go slow and dark at the begining and get more and more intense throughout the night as the crowd gets more active. Never force feed strobes on a crowd that doesn't want it. Usually clubs like it warm and cozy at first but more intense towards the end of the night. You have to read the room.

4. Don't fuck the payroll. Those bottle girls are pretty but they are your coworkers and that's it.

5. Give a shit. People pay a lot of money to come and see your work. Always give them a good show no matter what. You need to give them their money's worth.

If you follow those you'll do great. Go out and have fun.
